head_commit.message:
fix(browser-first): #509 fail-closed blocked-site snapshot on storage error

Address the review on 4aefe65.

[Important] The @tab typeahead failed OPEN on a failed permission read.
refreshBlockedSiteKeys read through sitePermissions(), which swallows a rejected
storage.get into {}, so a failed read set sitePermissionsLoaded = true with an
empty blocked set — every keyable site, including blocked ones, became listable
in the typeahead and resolvable as a mention (the page body was still refused).
Extract the snapshot + loaded flag into createBlockedSiteSnapshot, which takes the
site-permission STORE and reaches for its STRICT readSitePermissions by name: the
reader choice lives in the factory, so the lenient sitePermissions() cannot be
substituted at the call site, and the snapshot's siteKeyForUrl comes from the same
store so the two cannot drift. A store missing either method is rejected at
construction, so a miswire fails loudly rather than silently failing open. The
strict reader rejects on a failed read; on any error refresh() fails closed — the
loaded flag stays/returns to false, so the predicate withholds every keyable site
— then rethrows so the caller's .catch can log. side-panel.js hands the whole
store to the factory. Tests drive a REAL store whose storage.get rejects (not a
throwing stub) and assert nothing keyable is listed, plus a construction-guard
case, a later-rejection case, and a modelled broken-store control pinning why the
reader must reject; that readSitePermissions rejects while sitePermissions
swallows is pinned in site-permission-store.test.mjs.

[Minor] Parity test no longer exempts content's label-keep guard regexes: after
the #522 merge chat carries the same callback, so a straight subset check holds
and deleting the callback now turns both parity tests red. Added byte-exact
Authorization: Bearer/Basic expectations so the behavioural test pins that the
label survives (chat must not over-redact).

[Minor] A permission-blocked site's skip reason (posted into the transcript on
the compare path) now names the host only, never the blocked page's title or
path/query. Internal (non-http) tabs keep their existing label.

Checks: 11 affected browser-first unit lanes (readable-unblocked-tab,
readable-tab-ranking, tab-mention-typeahead, tab-context-controller,
tab-comparison-resolver, context-sanitizer-parity, chat-turn-controller,
site-permission-store, content-redaction, side-panel-command-wiring,
side-panel-dom) 130/130 pass; security-pipeline/run-check.mjs pass; repo:hygiene
0 credential findings; git diff --check clean.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
fix(dsh-native): close the final-gate findings on crash cleanup and home ancestry

Final review (Grok 4.7) found two Important defects. Both were confirmed in
code and are fixed here.

- After the owned child exits, cleanup no longer sends the session cookie.
  stop() runs beforeStop only while the child is alive. The native lease
  refuses cleanupUse once the child has exited. An in-flight cancel request
  aborts on child exit. Before this fix, a local process that bound the
  released port during the one-second cleanup window received the cookie.
- Every ancestor of the managed DSH home must be owned by root or the user
  and must not be group- or world-writable, the same rule the install prefix
  uses. The home's device and inode are re-verified before spawn, so a
  symlink swap to ~/.dsh is refused.

Also: the native binding refuses port 19387 (the desktop DSH port) in the
runtime and in the SDK validator, and the shared-readiness test now runs
through the real custody path instead of a fake lease.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
